lines.text: Princess Mirelle came down the steps alone, with her hands well away from her sword. Wren's arrow followed her all the way.
Put that down, archer. You still drop your left shoulder when you draw.
You still talk too much before a fight.
It was the friendliest thing either of them had ever said to the other.
After your fire, my uncle's guard went down into the vaults. I went with them. Nobody stops a princess. It's the only useful thing about being one.
I saw the farm, Lord Lucan. The beds. The glass. The children asleep with their eyes open.
She said it the way soldiers talk about a battle. Flat and fast, so it can't catch hold of them.
I asked you once why your people fight like they love you. Now I know what the rest of us keep in our cellars.
Then she saw Nell, asleep against Tamsin's shoulder. Mirelle had never knelt to anyone in her life. She knelt to Nell.
Are you a queen?
Not yet.
I can't help you openly. The court belongs to Vance, and my uncle belongs to whoever spoke to him last. If I move now, I'll be in a tower by morning.
So go home. Raise the north. Come back with an army, Lord Lucan, and I will open a door for you. From the inside.
Which door?
There's an old river door under the palace wall. Nobody has opened it since my grandmother was a girl. When you come, it will be open.
And how do I write to a princess without Vance reading it first?
I assumed you'd have an idea. You look like a man who has nothing but ideas.
The Charter of Aldric. Page, line and word. Every noble in Aldcrown learned the first page by heart. Nobody has ever read the rest.
I've never read past the first page.
That's what makes it a good code.
We shook hands on it in a cellar that smelled of dye. The King's niece, and the most wanted man in Aldmere.
Vance means to search the Lowmarket at dawn. Every house. Every cellar. Get out tonight, or not at all.
Then she pulled up her hood and was gone, and the cellar felt very small.
Seven people through a shut gate, my lord, with your face on every door. It can't be done.
You won't need the gate, my lord. The gate is going to be busy.
She smiled when she said it. It was the most frightening smile I saw in Aldcrown, and I had taken tea with Vance.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and eleven, coming soon.
